description: We are a passionate team of STEM school researchers with strong skills in web development, software, hardware prototyping, and technical content writing. With hands-on project experience, we complement each other to build impactful, end-to-end solutions. We welcome motivated teammates skilled in UI/UX, data analysis, or creative presentation to join our mission!
summary:
Bio Astro Lab (Orbital Observatory) is an offline-first, autonomous astronaut health triage and behavioral monitoring system built for deep-space missions (Moon/Artemis, Mars) where up to 22-minute communication delays prevent real-time ground support.

The platform combines a two-stage multimodal check-in—capturing manual/habitat vitals (glucose, BP, temperature, SpO2, sleep, mood, radiation, cabin CO2) alongside 3D webcam biomechanics (posture balance, 3-second rolling gait symmetry, pitch-compensated eye fatigue, and signal-quality-gated optical rPPG pulse)—with an on-device 1,650-tree XGBoost v3.0.0 classifier (92.99% test accuracy) running 100% locally in the browser. Unlike brittle clinical tools, Bio Astro Lab enforces a zero-fabrication telemetry policy, natively routing missing sensors (NaN) while guaranteeing safety through a deterministic NASA physiological guardrail.

Triage results drive an interactive 5-system astronaut hologram, explainable risk-driver breakdowns, a 13-slider What-If simulator, an offline 48-document NASA HRP protocol assistant, and a conversational psychological companion that detects "stoic masking" by fusing dialogue with biometric strain.
details:
What It Does & How It Works
Bio Astro Lab (Orbital Observatory) is an offline-first, autonomous astronaut health triage and psychological monitoring platform designed for deep-space missions (Moon/Artemis, Deep Transit, and Mars) where up to 22-minute communication delays prevent continuous real-time support from Earth flight surgeons.


The system operates across four integrated stages:

  1. Two-Stage Zero-Fabrication Check-In: In Stage 1, crew members log up to nine clinical and habitat metrics (blood glucose, blood pressure, core temperature, heart rate, SpO2, sleep duration, mood score, ionizing radiation dose, and cabin CO2). Any unmeasured metric stays strictly NaN rather than being auto-filled with synthetic defaults. In Stage 2, a standard webcam captures 3D pose and facial landmarks at 30 Hz to measure posture/balance, 3-second rolling gait range-of-motion (ROM) symmetry, pitch-compensated Eye Aspect Ratio (EAR) fatigue, and an experimental forehead optical heart rate (CHROM rPPG) gated by a spectral Signal Quality Index (SQI >= 50%).
  2. On-Device Edge AI Triage: All 13 features pass directly into a 1,650-tree XGBoost v3.0.0 classifier (92.99% accuracy, 0.9851 Macro ROC-AUC on an unseen subject-disjoint test set) compiled into pure browser JavaScript. The model natively routes missing (NaN) sensors via IEEE-754 floating-point splits and pairs ML probabilities with a deterministic monotonic clinical safety floor grounded in NASA-STD-3001 thresholds so life-threatening spikes (such as cabin CO2 >= 4.0 mmHg or SpO2 < 90%) always trigger an immediate Critical alert.
  3. Explainable Decision Support & Longitudinal Tracking: Triage outputs power an interactive 5-system astronaut hologram (brain, heart, lungs, metabolic core, muscles), SHAP-style counterfactual risk-driver charts, a 13-slider live What-If simulator, longitudinal trend charts with formula-safe CSV exports, an offline 48-document NASA Human Research Program (HRP) RAG guide, and 6 emergency SOS protocols.
  4. Multimodal Psychological Check-In & Stoic-Masking Detection: A local FastAPI companion (<astro-chat>) conducts structured 7-turn conversational check-ins and fuses dialogue scores with physiological, facial, and acoustic telemetry against per-astronaut Welford online baselines.
Key Benefits

  • 100% Earth-Independent Autonomy: Every inference tree, emergency checklist, trend plot, and NASA reference lookup executes locally without cloud connectivity.
  • Resilience to Partial Sensor Dropouts: Eliminates false alarms or silent crashes when blood labs, wearables, or cameras are unavailable.
  • Early Detection of Hidden Distress: Identifies "channel conflicts" when an astronaut minimizes stress verbally despite elevated autonomic, vocal, or facial strain, alerting flight surgeons after three consecutive deviant sessions or acute safety triggers.
  • Transparent & Actionable Guidance: Gives crew members clear per-organ explanations and interactive "What-If" countermeasures rather than opaque black-box scores.
Intended Impact
Bio Astro Lab directly addresses NASA's five RIDGE spaceflight hazards (Radiation, Isolation & Confinement, Distance from Earth, Gravity Fields, and Hostile/Closed Environments) by shifting crew healthcare from reactive, ground-dependent telemedicine to proactive, onboard clinical autonomy. Beyond deep-space habitats, Lunar rovers, and orbital stations, its offline missing-sensor architecture and low-cost webcam biomechanics can extend clinical decision support to remote terrestrial analog environments, polar stations, maritime vessels, and underserved rural clinics with intermittent connectivity.


Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Frontend & On-Device Inference: HTML5, CSS3, Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+), MediaPipe Tasks Vision (PoseLandmarker & FaceLandmarker), Chart.js 4, GSAP 3 + ScrollTrigger, Lenis, and Web Components (Shadow DOM).
  • Machine Learning & Data Engineering: Python 3, XGBoost (v3.0.0), NumPy, Pandas, SciPy, Scikit-Learn (StratifiedGroupKFold), and automated headless Chromium V8 parity testing (unittest).
  • Backend & Conversational RAG Microservice: Python FastAPI, SQLite with FTS5 (BM25 full-text search), SQLAlchemy, Pydantic, Pytest, and pluggable LLM clients (Anthropic Claude, Gemini, Groq, OpenRouter, Ollama, plus deterministic offline mock mode).
  • Datasets & Scientific Standards: Trained and validated across CDC NHANES, PhysioNet CinC Challenge 2012 ICU cohorts, PhysioNet Human Balance Evaluation Database, OpenML EEG Eye State, NASA OSDR SpaceX Inspiration4 (OSD-575) human crew labs, and NASA HRP / NASA-STD-3001 physiological guidelines.
  • Hardware: Standard consumer laptop/workstation CPU and integrated 30 Hz RGB webcam (zero specialized clinical hardware required for inference).
How Our Project Is Creative

  • Anti-Shortcut Missingness Engineering: Multi-cohort medical AI models often cheat by memorizing which dataset a missing feature came from. We solved this via subject-disjoint splitting combined with class-conditional bitmask equalization, driving missingness-to-target correlation down to Cramér's V = 0.0366 so the model learns true physiology rather than sensor availability.
  • Locomotion-Safe 3D Camera Kinematics: Instead of fragile 2D bounding-box checks that fail when an astronaut walks sideways or paces in front of a camera, we engineered yaw-angle gating, horizontal-translation-invariant posture scoring, 3-second rolling gait ROM symmetry, and pitch-compensated eye fatigue tracking.
  • Hybrid AI + Monotonic Safety Barrier: Combining gradient-boosted trees with a declarative clinical envelope gives crews nuanced multi-vital pattern recognition while mathematically preventing dangerous edge cases from being averaged into a false "Optimal" clearance.
  • Dual-Channel Stoic Masking Fusion: Cross-checking self-reported mood against objective physiological and facial baselines tackles one of spaceflight's hardest human-factors blind spots.
Key Factors Our Team Considered

  • Zero-Fabrication Ethics & Safety: Camera denial or unentered lab values never silently fabricate healthy numbers; synthetic playback is strictly opt-in and explicitly labeled.
  • Biological & Data Integrity: We enforced strict subject-disjoint splits (zero subject overlap between train and test), quarantined non-human/rodent OSDR datasets (manifest.json), neutralized SAS XPORT sentinel artifacts, and validated generalization against never-seen ICU clinical severity scores (SAPS-I and SOFA).
  • Human Factors & Cognitive Load: Designed an "Orbital Observatory" high-contrast UI (tabular-nums telemetry HUDs paired with calm archival clinical cards) that surfaces immediate red flags, bilingual English/Arabic support, and concise countermeasures without inducing alarm fatigue during high-stress mission operations.
